MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 26, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC) Executive Director Adrienne
Mohan and Randy Harwood, Executive Vice President of the PVPLC Board of Directors.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Michael Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson
  Senior Accountant Fernando Estrada

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING SEPTEMBER 2025 "NATIONAL PREPAREDNESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR STEGURA declared September 2025 as “National Preparedness Month.”

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ requested to abstain from voting on Consent Calendar items
5F, having not been present at that meeting.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-I AS FOLLOWS
  BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Schmitz (5F)

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF AUGUST 2025

  APPROVED WARRANTS 68669 THROUGH 68852 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $1,064,460.87 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 070725 THROUGH
  070825; 080125 THROUGH 080325; IN THE AMOUNT OF $242,713.49; FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,307,174.36 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
AUGUST 26, 2025
 C.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF JULY 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF JULY 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  BUDGET AMENDMENTS FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025

  APPROVED THE BUDGET AMENDMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JULY 22, 2025

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JULY 28, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  CONTRACT LAW COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 8, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  2025 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JANUARY 1, 2025 TO AUGUST
  1, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE – 3RD QUARTER 2025

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 3 Silver Spring Drive
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: CVS, Silver Spur Road

Public comment was also received from Torrance resident Alan Fradkin, regarding concerns
about pickleball court reservations and court maintenance.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 250169
  AMENDMENT AND RESTATEMENT OF CHAPTER 17.56 OF THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO ACCESSORY
  DWELLING UNITS
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Open the continued public hearing and take
  public testimony; 2) Discuss Ordinance No. 752; 3) Close the public hearing; and 4)
  Conduct the second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 752.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, to open the public hearing.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, to close the public hearing.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 26, 2025
   CONDUCT SECOND READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 752.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 752 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: NATURE CENTER
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA LAND
  CONSERVANCY

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached Interim Agreement for
  Nature Center Services with the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that maintenance is performed in combination with
City staff, PVPLC staff and volunteers, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE INTERIM AGREEMENT FOR NATURE CENTER SERVICES
  WITH THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA LAND CONSERVANCY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER PROJECT UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to proceed with soliciting bids for
  Phase One of the Nature Center Project (main building construct, excluding the
  walkway and outdoor classroom) and authorize staff to pursue financing options to
  close the remaining funding gap.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), including
an outline of the project timeline, overview of the project, estimated costs, funds
allocated/identified and the funding gap.

Senior Accountant Estrada then introduced consultant Mark Young from KNN Public Finance,
who provided a presentation outlining Nature Center Financing Options.

Discussion ensued about consideration of the three proposed finance options: 1) Pay-Go
utilizing reserve funds; 2) Lease financing via a direct placement with a commercial bank; and
3) Hybrid Approach: Reimbursement Resolution to utilize both pay-go and debt financing.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided an update on small donor efforts, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN confirmed that the total funds allocated of $5M includes
professional services that have already been spent. He also confirmed that the “debt” in the
hybrid approach is an optional, and the money does not have to be borrowed if it’s not needed.
Lastly, he confirmed that the estimated $1.1M of reserve funds would be the last money spent.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 26, 2025
 Assistant City Manager Davis explained what “forward progress” looks like regarding the grant
Senator Allen helped the City receive, in response to MAYOR STEGURA.

City Manager Grammer noted that the estimate includes a $500,000 contingency for
unforeseen project expenses and believes there will be grant fund opportunities available for
the second phase of the project as well, which staff plans to pursue.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO PROCEED WITH SOLICITING BIDS FOR PHASE ONE
  OF THE NATURE CENTER PROJECT (MAIN BUILDING CONSTRUCT,
  EXCLUDING THE WALKWAY AND OUTDOOR CLASSROOM).

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO PURSUE THE HYBRID FINANCING APPROACH USING
  PAY-GO FUNDING AND DEBT FINANCING OPTIONS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended a meeting with the City of Hawthorne & Mexico Counsel
General last week, and thanked Council and staff for attending her installation ceremony as
President for the Los Angeles Division of Cal Cities on August 7.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER attended the Cal Water Emergency Operations workshop
this month.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN will be attending the California Contract Cities Association’s
Fall Educational Seminar in September. He also yielded his position on the Southern California
Association of Governments (SCAG) Community, Economic, & Human Development (CEHD)
Committee, and was then asked to be a Presidential Appointee to the Committee.

MAYOR STEGURA attended the quarterly meetings for the Peninsula Public Safety
Committee and Regional Contract Law Committee in August.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  LETTER OF SUPPORT TO EXPAND EXECUTIVE ORDER N-32-25 TO INCLUDE
  THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA IN SUSPENDING SB 9 APPLICATIONS WITHIN
  VERY HIGH FIRE HAZARD SEVERITY ZONES

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the Letter of
  Support to expand Executive Order N-32-25 to include the Palos Verdes Peninsula
  region in suspending SB 9 applications within Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
AUGUST 26, 2025
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE LETTER OF SUPPORT TO
  EXPAND EXECUTIVE ORDER N-32-25 TO INCLUDE THE PALOS VERDES
  PENINSULA REGION IN SUSPENDING SB 9 APPLICATIONS WITHIN VERY
  HIGH FIRE HAZARD SEVERITY ZONES.

MAYOR STEGURA so ordered.

B.  DESIGNATION OF VOTING DELEGATES AND ALTERNATES FOR CAL CITIES
  ANNUAL CONFERENCE & EXPO

  DELEGATE:  COUNCIL MEMBER BRITT HUFF
  ALTERNATE:  MAYOR STEGURA

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Annual Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:42 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting in memory former City employee
Ellen Shinkai.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
AUGUST 26, 2025
